summary.objective: Decide whether to retain and investigate the current J12 connector or evaluate a replacement, without changing the board pinout.
summary.headline: Intermittent J12 disconnects under vibration are reported but unmeasured; no vibration test, retention data, candidate datasheet or independent review exists, so no connector change can be approved yet.

sourceRegister.name: Field observation note — Rover Alpha J12 (synthetic)

anchors.excerpt: Operators reported intermittent J12 connector disconnects during vibration on the test track on three separate days.
Each report describes the drive controller losing its link to the sensor harness for one to three seconds and then recovering.
No vibration profile, accelerometer data or connector retention measurement was recorded.
The reports do not identify whether the J12 shell, the contacts or the harness strain relief released.
Constraint R1: Any connector change must preserve the existing board pinout so the controller firmware and the sensor harness remain unchanged.
Constraint R2: The replacement, if any, must be compatible with the existing drive controller board footprint.
The exact baseline revision of the controller board is not supplied in this note.
The pin mapping table and the compatibility measurements for any candidate connector are not supplied in this note.
Checklist item 1: Vibration-test result for the current J12 connector — ABSENT. No vibration test has been run or recorded.
Checklist item 2: Connector retention-force measurement — not recorded.
Checklist item 3: Candidate replacement connector datasheet — not supplied.
Checklist item 4: Independent engineering review — an independent engineering reviewer has not approved the change.

alternatives.title: Retain and investigate current J12 connector
alternatives.description: Keep the existing J12 and determine the failure mode (shell, contacts or strain relief) through vibration testing and retention measurement. Effectiveness is unknown until evidenced.
prerequisites: Defined vibration profile and vibration test of current J12

alternatives.title: Evaluate a replacement connector
alternatives.description: Evaluate a candidate connector that preserves pinout and footprint. No candidate is named; compatibility is unknown until evidenced.

affectedArtifacts.label: Drive controller board pinout / footprint

reviewQuestions.question: What vibration profile represents the test track, and can the disconnect be reproduced on the current J12?
Which element released: J12 shell, contacts or harness strain relief?
What is the controller board baseline revision and its J12 pin mapping?
Does any candidate connector have a datasheet and measured footprint/pinout compatibility?

nextAction.action: Define a test-track vibration profile and run an instrumented vibration test with retention-force measurement on the current J12 before any change decision.
nextAction.requiredInput: Vibration profile, current board baseline revision, retention test setup

limitations: Packet ready means the paid preparation artifact was delivered. It is not engineering approval, a completed test or permission to release hardware. Independent engineering review and relevant physical evidence remain required.
All sources are labeled synthetic fixtures invented for demonstration; statements are recorded with kind 'synthetic fixture'.
No measurements, test results or part numbers were supplied; none are asserted.
The field lead's recommendation to investigate a change is recorded as content, not as approval.
